shloka_text: प्रविष्टायां हुताशं तु वेदवत्यां स रावणः । पुष्पकं तु समारुह्य परिचक्राम मेदिनीम् ।। 7.18.1 ।।
transliteration: praviṣṭāyāṃ hutāśaṃ tu vedavatyāṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ | puṣpakaṃ tu samāruhya paricakrāma medinīm || 7.18.1 ||
translation: प्रविष्टायां having entered, हुताशं fire, तु indeed, वेदवत्यां Vedavati, सः he, रावणः Ravana, पुष्पकं Pushpaka (chariot), तु indeed, समारुह्य having ascended, परिचक्राम wandered around, मेदिनीम् the earth.
explanation: After Vedavati entered the fire, Ravana ascended his Pushpaka chariot and wandered across the earth.
comments: Ravana comes upon King Marutta's sacrifice, where the terrified gods hide in animal forms -- Indra as a peacock, Yama as a crow, Kubera as a lizard and Varuna as a swan -- restrained by the sage Samvarta from breaking his consecration, Marutta does not fight, and Ravana, proclaimed victor, devours the assembled sages and departs -- the gods resume their forms and bless the creatures whose shapes they had taken.

shloka_text: ततो मरुत्तं नृपतिं यजन्तं सह दैवतैः । उशीरबीजमासाद्य ददर्श स तु रावणः ।। 7.18.2 ।।
transliteration: tato maruttaṃ nṛpatiṃ yajantaṃ saha daivataiḥ | uśīrabījamāsādya dadarśa sa tu rāvaṇaḥ || 7.18.2 ||
translation: ततः then, मरुत्तं Marutta, नृपतिं king, यजन्तं sacrificing, सह with, दैवतैः deities, उशीरबीजम् Ushirabija (a place), आसाद्य having reached, ददर्श saw, सः he, तु indeed, रावणः Ravana.
explanation: Then, having arrived at Ushirabija, Ravana saw King Marutta performing a sacrifice with the deities.

shloka_text: संवर्तो नाम ब्रह्मर्षिः साक्षाद्भ्राता बृहस्पतेः । याजयामास धर्मज्ञः सर्वैर्देवगणैर्वृतः ।। 7.18.3 ।।
transliteration: saṃvarto nāma brahmarṣiḥ sākṣādbhrātā bṛhaspateḥ | yājayāmāsa dharmajñaḥ sarvairdevagaṇairvṛtaḥ || 7.18.3 ||
translation: संवर्तः Samvarta, नाम named, ब्रह्मर्षिः a Brahmarshi (sage), साक्षात् directly, भ्राता brother, बृहस्पतेः of Brihaspati, याजयामास officiated (the sacrifice), धर्मज्ञः knower of dharma, सर्वैः all, देवगणैः hosts of gods, वृतः surrounded by.
explanation: The righteous Brahmarshi named Samvarta, who was the direct brother of Brihaspati, officiated the sacrifice, surrounded by all the hosts of gods.

shloka_text: दृष्ट्वा देवास्तु तद्रक्षो वरदानेन दुर्जयम् । तिर्यग्योनिं समाविष्टास्तस्य दर्शनभीरवः ।। 7.18.4 ।।
transliteration: dṛṣṭvā devāstu tadrakṣo varadānena durjayam | tiryagyoniṃ samāviṣṭāstasya darśanabhīravaḥ || 7.18.4 ||
translation: दृष्ट्वा having seen, देवाः the gods, तु indeed, तत् that, रक्षः demon, वरदानेन by the boon, दुर्जयम् unconquerable, तिर्यग्योनिं animal forms, समाविष्टाः entered, तस्य his, दर्शनभीरवः fearful of the sight.
explanation: The gods, fearful of the sight of that demon who was unconquerable due to a boon, assumed animal forms.

shloka_text: इन्द्रो मयूरः संवृत्तो धर्मराजस्तु वायसः । कृकलासो धनाध्यक्षो हंसश्च वरुणो ऽभवत् ।। 7.18.5 ।।
transliteration: indro mayūraḥ saṃvṛtto dharmarājastu vāyasaḥ | kṛkalāso dhanādhyakṣo haṃsaśca varuṇo 'bhavat || 7.18.5 ||
translation: इन्द्रो Indra, मयूरः a peacock, संवृत्तो became, धर्मराजस्तु Dharma-raja (Yama) and, वायसः a crow, कृकलासो a chameleon, धनाध्यक्षो the lord of wealth (Kubera), हंसश्च a swan and, वरुणो Varuna, ऽभवत् became
explanation: Indra transformed into a peacock, Yama into a crow, Kubera into a chameleon, and Varuna into a swan.

shloka_text: अन्येष्वपि गतेष्वेवं देवेष्वरिनिषूदन । रावणः प्राविशद्यज्ञं सारमेय इवाशुचिः ।। 7.18.6 ।।
transliteration: anyeṣvapi gateṣvevaṃ deveṣvariniṣūdana | rāvaṇaḥ prāviśadyajñaṃ sārameya ivāśuciḥ || 7.18.6 ||
translation: अन्येष्वपि even among others, गतेष्वेवं having gone thus, देवेषु among the gods, अरिनिषूदन O destroyer of enemies, रावणः Ravana, प्राविशत् entered, यज्ञं the sacrifice, सारमेय a dog, इव like, अशुचिः impure
explanation: O destroyer of enemies, while other gods had also transformed and departed, Ravana entered the sacrifice like an impure dog.

shloka_text: तं च राजानमासाद्य रावणो राक्षसाधिपः । प्राह युद्धं प्रयच्छेति निर्जितो ऽस्मीति वा वद ।। 7.18.7 ।।
transliteration: taṃ ca rājānamāsādya rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ | prāha yuddhaṃ prayaccheti nirjito 'smīti vā vada || 7.18.7 ||
translation: तं him, च and, राजानम् the king, आसाद्य having approached, रावणो Ravana, राक्षसाधिपः the lord of Rakshasas, प्राह said, युद्धं battle, प्रयच्छेति give (me), निर्जितो conquered, ऽस्मीति I am, वा or, वद say
explanation: And having approached that king, Ravana, the lord of Rakshasas, said, "Either give me battle, or declare that I am conquered."

shloka_text: ततो मरुत्तो नृपतिः को भवानित्युवाच तम् । अपहासं ततो मुक्त्वा रावणो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।। 7.18.8 ।।
transliteration: tato marutto nṛpatiḥ ko bhavānityuvāca tam | apahāsaṃ tato muktvā rāvaṇo vākyamabravīt || 7.18.8 ||
translation: ततो then, मरुत्तो Marutta, नृपतिः the king, को who, भवान् are you, इति thus, उवाच said, तम् to him, अपहासं a scornful laugh, ततो then, मुक्त्वा having let out, रावणो Ravana, वाक्यम् words, अब्रवीत् spoke
explanation: Then King Marutta asked him, "Who are you?", whereupon Ravana, letting out a scornful laugh, spoke these words.

shloka_text: अकुतूहलभावेन प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव पार्थिव । धनदस्यानुजं यो मां नावगच्छसि रावणम् ।। 7.18.9 ।।
transliteration: akutūhalabhāvena prīto 'smi tava pārthiva | dhanadasyānujaṃ yo māṃ nāvagacchasi rāvaṇam || 7.18.9 ||
translation: अकुतूहलभावेन by your lack of curiosity, प्रीतो pleased, ऽस्मि I am, तव your, पार्थिव O king, धनदस्य of Kubera, अनुजं the younger brother, यो who, मां me, न not, अवगच्छसि you recognize, रावणम् Ravana
explanation: Ravana said, "O king, I am pleased by your lack of curiosity, as you do not recognize me, Ravana, the younger brother of Kubera."

shloka_text: त्रिषु लोकेषु को ऽन्यो ऽस्ति यो न जानाति मे बलम् । भ्रातरं येन निर्जित्य विमानमिदमाहृतम् । ततो मरुत्तः स नृपस्तं रावणमथाब्रवीत् ।। 7.18.10 ।।
transliteration: triṣu lokeṣu ko 'nyo 'sti yo na jānāti me balam | bhrātaraṃ yena nirjitya vimānamidamāhṛtam | tato maruttaḥ sa nṛpastaṃ rāvaṇamathābravīt || 7.18.10 ||
translation: त्रिषु in three, लोकेषु worlds, कः who, अन्यः other, अस्ति is, यः who, न not, जानाति knows, मे my, बलम् strength, भ्रातरम् brother, येन by whom, निर्जित्य having conquered, विमानम् aerial chariot, इदम् this, आहृतम् was brought, ततः then, मरुत्तः Marutta, सः that, नृपः king, तम् to him, रावणम् to Ravana, अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Ravana boasts, "Who in the three worlds does not know my strength, by which I conquered my brother and brought this aerial chariot?"; then King Marutta spoke to Ravana.

shloka_text: धन्यः खलु भवान्येन ज्येष्ठो भ्राता रणे जितः । न त्वया सदृशः श्लाध्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते ।। 7.18.11 ।।
transliteration: dhanyaḥ khalu bhavānyena jyeṣṭho bhrātā raṇe jitaḥ | na tvayā sadṛśaḥ ślādhyastriṣu lokeṣu vidyate || 7.18.11 ||
translation: धन्यः blessed, खलु indeed, भवान् you, येन by whom, ज्येष्ठः elder, भ्राता brother, रणे in battle, जितः was conquered, न not, त्वया by you, सदृशः similar, श्लाध्यः praiseworthy, त्रिषु in three, लोकेषु worlds, विद्यते exists.
explanation: Marutta sarcastically remarks, "Indeed, you are blessed, by whom the elder brother was conquered in battle; there is no one praiseworthy like you in the three worlds."

shloka_text: नाधर्मसहितं श्लाध्यं तल्लोकं प्रतिसंहितम् । कर्म दौरात्म्यकं कृत्वा श्लाघ्यसे भ्रातृनिर्जयात् ।। 7.18.12 ।।
transliteration: nādharmasahitaṃ ślādhyaṃ tallokaṃ pratisaṃhitam | karma daurātmyakaṃ kṛtvā ślāghyase bhrātṛnirjayāt || 7.18.12 ||
translation: न not, अधर्मसहितम् associated with unrighteousness, श्लाध्यम् praiseworthy, तत् that, लोकम् people, प्रतिसंहितम् connected to, कर्म act, दौरात्म्यकम् wicked, कृत्वा having done, श्लाघ्यसे you boast, भ्रातृनिर्जयात् from conquering a brother.
explanation: Marutta continues, "An act associated with unrighteousness is not praiseworthy among people; having performed such a wicked deed, you boast about conquering your brother."

shloka_text: क त्वं प्राक्केवलं धर्मं चरित्वा लब्धवान्वरम् । श्रूतपूर्वं हि न मया भाषसे यादृशं स्वयम् ।। 7.18.13 ।।
transliteration: ka tvaṃ prākkevalaṃ dharmaṃ caritvā labdhavānvaram | śrūtapūrvaṃ hi na mayā bhāṣase yādṛśaṃ svayam || 7.18.13 ||
translation: क how, त्वम् you, प्राक् formerly, केवलम् only, धर्मम् righteousness, चरित्वा having practiced, लब्धवान् obtained, वरम् boon, श्रूतपूर्वं heard before, हि indeed, न not, मया by me, भाषसे you speak, यादृशम् such as, स्वयम् yourself.
explanation: Marutta questions, "How did you, who formerly practiced only righteousness, obtain a boon? Indeed, I have never heard you speak such words as you now utter."

shloka_text: तिष्ठेदानीं न मे जीवन्प्रतियास्यसि दुर्मते । अद्य त्वां निशितैर्बाणैः प्रेषयामि यमक्षयम् ।। 7.18.14 ।।
transliteration: tiṣṭhedānīṃ na me jīvanpratiyāsyasi durmate | adya tvāṃ niśitairbāṇaiḥ preṣayāmi yamakṣayam || 7.18.14 ||
translation: तिष्ठ stop, इदानीम् now, न not, मे from me, जीवन् living, प्रतियास्यसि you will return, दुर्मते O evil-minded one, अद्य today, त्वाम् you, निशितैः sharp, बाणैः with arrows, प्रेषयामि I send, यमक्षयम् to Yama's abode.
explanation: Marutta declares, "Stop now, O evil-minded one, you will not return alive from me; today I will send you to Yama's abode with sharp arrows."

shloka_text: ततः शरासनं गृह्य सायकांश्च नराधिपः । रणाय निर्ययौ क्रुद्धः संवर्तो मार्गमावृणोत् ।। 7.18.15 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ śarāsanaṃ gṛhya sāyakāṃśca narādhipaḥ | raṇāya niryayau kruddhaḥ saṃvarto mārgamāvṛṇot || 7.18.15 ||
translation: ततः then, शरासनं bow, गृह्य having taken, सायकांश्च and arrows, नराधिपः the king, रणाय for battle, निर्ययौ went forth, क्रुद्धः enraged, संवर्तो Samvarta, मार्गम् the path, आवृणोत् blocked.
explanation: Then, the enraged King Marutta, having taken his bow and arrows, went forth for battle, but the sage Samvarta blocked his path.

shloka_text: सो ऽब्रवीत्स्नेहसंयुक्तं मरुत्तं तं महानृषिः । श्रोतव्यं यदि मद्वाक्यं सम्प्रहारो न ते क्षमः ।। 7.18.16 ।।
transliteration: so 'bravītsnehasaṃyuktaṃ maruttaṃ taṃ mahānṛṣiḥ | śrotavyaṃ yadi madvākyaṃ samprahāro na te kṣamaḥ || 7.18.16 ||
translation: सः he, अब्रवीत् spoke, स्नेहसंयुक्तं affectionately, मरुत्तं to Marutta, तं that, महानृषिः great sage, श्रोतव्यं should be heard, यदि if, मद्वाक्यं my words, सम्प्रहारो battle, न not, ते for you, क्षमः suitable.
explanation: That great sage Samvarta affectionately spoke to Marutta, saying that if his words were to be heard, then battle was not suitable for him.

shloka_text: माहेश्वरमिदं सत्रमसमाप्तं कुलं दहेत् ।। 7.18.17 ।।
transliteration: māheśvaramidaṃ satramasamāptaṃ kulaṃ dahet || 7.18.17 ||
translation: इदं this, माहेश्वरम् सत्रम् sacrifice dedicated to Maheshvara, असमाप्तम् if left unfinished, कुलं the lineage, दहेत् would consume.
explanation: This sacrifice dedicated to Maheshvara, if left unfinished, would consume the whole lineage.

shloka_text: दीक्षितस्य कुतो युद्धं क्रोधित्वं दीक्षिते कुतः । संशयश्च जये नित्यं राक्षसश्च सुदुर्जयः ।। 7.18.18 ।।
transliteration: dīkṣitasya kuto yuddhaṃ krodhitvaṃ dīkṣite kutaḥ | saṃśayaśca jaye nityaṃ rākṣasaśca sudurjayaḥ || 7.18.18 ||
translation: दीक्षितस्य for one who is consecrated, कुतो whence, युद्धं battle, क्रोधित्वं anger, दीक्षिते in one who is consecrated, कुतः whence, संशयश्च and doubt, जये in victory, नित्यं always, राक्षसश्च and the demon, सुदुर्जयः very difficult to conquer.
explanation: For one consecrated for a sacrifice, whence comes battle, and whence comes anger; moreover, there is always doubt in victory, and the demon is very difficult to conquer.

shloka_text: स निवृत्तो गुरोर्वाक्यान्मरुत्तः पृथिवीपतिः । विसृज्य सशरं चापं स्वस्थो मखमुखो ऽभवत् ।। 7.18.19 ।।
transliteration: sa nivṛtto gurorvākyānmaruttaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ | visṛjya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ svastho makhamukho 'bhavat || 7.18.19 ||
translation: सः he, निवृत्तो turned back, गुरोर्वाक्यात् from the guru's words, मरुत्तः Marutta, पृथिवीपतिः the king, विसृज्य having abandoned, सशरं with arrows, चापं the bow, स्वस्थो composed, मखमुखो intent on the sacrifice, अभवत् became.
explanation: Following his guru's words, King Marutta turned back, abandoned his bow and arrows, and became composed and intent on his sacrifice.

shloka_text: ततस्तं निर्जितं मत्वा घोषयामास वै शुकः । रावणो जयतीत्युच्चैर्हर्षान्नादं विमुक्तवान् ।। 7.18.20 ।।
transliteration: tatastaṃ nirjitaṃ matvā ghoṣayāmāsa vai śukaḥ | rāvaṇo jayatītyuccairharṣānnādaṃ vimuktavān || 7.18.20 ||
translation: ततः then, तं him, निर्जितं defeated, मत्वा having considered, घोषयामास announced, वै indeed, शुकः Shuka, रावणो Ravana, जयति is victorious, इति thus, उच्चैः loudly, हर्षात् from joy, नादं a proclamation, विमुक्तवान् uttered.
explanation: Then, Shuka, considering Marutta defeated, loudly proclaimed with joy, "Ravana is victorious!"

shloka_text: तान्भक्षयित्वा तत्रस्थान्महर्षीन्यज्ञमागतान् । वितृप्तो रुधिरैस्तेषां पुनः सम्प्रययौ महीम् ।। 7.18.21 ।।
transliteration: tānbhakṣayitvā tatrasthānmaharṣīnyajñamāgatān | vitṛpto rudhiraisteṣāṃ punaḥ samprayayau mahīm || 7.18.21 ||
translation: तान् them, भक्षयित्वा having devoured, तत्रस्थान् who were there, महर्षीन् great sages, यज्ञम् to the sacrifice, आगतान् who had come, वितृप्तः fully satisfied, रुधिरैः with the blood, तेषाम् of them, पुनः again, सम्प्रययौ he went, महीम् to the earth.
explanation: Having devoured those great sages who had come to the sacrifice and were there, and being fully satisfied with their blood, he again went to the earth.

shloka_text: रावणे तु गते देवाः सेन्द्राश्चैव दिवौकसः । ततः स्वां योनिमासाद्य तानि सत्त्वानि चाब्रुवन् ।। 7.18.22 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇe tu gate devāḥ sendrāścaiva divaukasaḥ | tataḥ svāṃ yonimāsādya tāni sattvāni cābruvan || 7.18.22 ||
translation: रावणे when Ravana, तु indeed, गते had gone, देवाः the gods, सेन्द्राः with Indra, च and, एव indeed, दिवौकसः the dwellers of heaven, ततः then, स्वाम् their own, योनिम् form, आसाद्य having attained, तानि to those, सत्त्वानि beings, च and, अब्रुवन् they spoke.
explanation: When Ravana had indeed gone, the gods, along with Indra and other dwellers of heaven, then regained their own forms and spoke to those beings.

shloka_text: हर्षात्तदाब्रवीदिन्द्रो मयूरं नीलबर्हिणम् । प्रीतो ऽस्मि तव धर्मज्ञ भुजङ्गाद्धि न ते भयम् ।। 7.18.23 ।।
transliteration: harṣāttadābravīdindro mayūraṃ nīlabarhiṇam | prīto 'smi tava dharmajña bhujaṅgāddhi na te bhayam || 7.18.23 ||
translation: हर्षात् from joy, तदा then, अब्रवीत् spoke, इन्द्रः Indra, मयूरम् to the peacock, नीलबर्हिणम् with blue feathers, प्रीतः pleased, अस्मि I am, तव with you, धर्मज्ञ O knower of dharma, भुजङ्गात् from serpents, हि indeed, न not, ते to you, भयम् fear.
explanation: Then, from joy, Indra spoke to the blue-feathered peacock, saying, "O knower of dharma, I am pleased with you, and indeed, you shall have no fear from serpents."

shloka_text: इदं नेत्रसहस्रं तु यत्त्वद्बर्हे भविष्यति । वर्षमाणे मयि मुदं प्राप्स्यसे प्रीतिलक्षणाम् । एवमिन्द्रो वरं प्रादान्मयूरस्य सुरेश्वरः ।। 7.18.24 ।।
transliteration: idaṃ netrasahasraṃ tu yattvadbarhe bhaviṣyati | varṣamāṇe mayi mudaṃ prāpsyase prītilakṣaṇām | evamindro varaṃ prādānmayūrasya sureśvaraḥ || 7.18.24 ||
translation: इदम् this, नेत्रसहस्रम् thousand eyes, तु indeed, यत् which, त्वद्बर्हे on your tail-feathers, भविष्यति will be, वर्षमाणे while raining, मयि by me, मुदम् joy, प्राप्स्यसे you will obtain, प्रीतिलक्षणाम् marked by pleasure, एवम् thus, इन्द्रः Indra, वरम् a boon, प्रादात् gave, मयूरस्य to the peacock, सुरेश्वरः the lord of gods.
explanation: Indra, the lord of gods, thus granted a boon to the peacock, saying that the thousand eyes would appear on its tail-feathers, and it would experience joy, a sign of pleasure, when he (Indra) rained.

shloka_text: नीलाः किल पुरा बर्हा मयूराणां नराधिप । सुराधिपाद्वरं प्राप्य गताः सर्वे ऽपि बर्हिणः ।। 7.18.25 ।।
transliteration: nīlāḥ kila purā barhā mayūrāṇāṃ narādhipa | surādhipādvaraṃ prāpya gatāḥ sarve 'pi barhiṇaḥ || 7.18.25 ||
translation: नीलाः blue, किल it is said, पुरा formerly, बर्हाः feathers, मयूराणाम् of peacocks, नराधिप O king of men, सुराधिपात् from the lord of gods, वरम् a boon, प्राप्य having obtained, गताः they became, सर्वे all, अपि even, बर्हिणः peacocks.
explanation: O king of men, it is said that formerly the feathers of peacocks were blue, and having obtained a boon from the lord of gods, all peacocks became (as they are now, with the characteristic 'eyes' on their feathers).

shloka_text: धर्मराजो ऽब्रवीद्राम प्राग्वंशे वायसं स्थितम् । पक्षिंस्तवास्मि सुप्रीतः प्रीतस्य वचनं शृणु ।। 7.18.26 ।।
transliteration: dharmarājo 'bravīdrāma prāgvaṃśe vāyasaṃ sthitam | pakṣiṃstavāsmi suprītaḥ prītasya vacanaṃ śṛṇu || 7.18.26 ||
translation: धर्मराजो Dharmaraja, अब्रवीत् said, राम O Rama, प्राग्वंशे in the eastern part of the house, वायसं to the crow, स्थितम् situated, पक्षिंस्तवास्मि O bird, I am, सुप्रीतः very pleased, प्रीतस्य of the pleased one, वचनं words, शृणु listen.
explanation: Dharmaraja (Yama) addressed the crow, who was formerly Rama, situated in the eastern part of the house, saying, "O bird, I am very pleased with you; listen to the words of one who is pleased."

shloka_text: यथान्ये विविधै रोगै; पीड्यन्ते प्राणिनो मया । ते न ते प्रभविष्यन्ति मयि प्रीते न संशयः ।। 7.18.27 ।।
transliteration: yathānye vividhai rogai; pīḍyante prāṇino mayā | te na te prabhaviṣyanti mayi prīte na saṃśayaḥ || 7.18.27 ||
translation: यथा just as, अन्ये others, विविधै by various, रोगैः diseases, पीड्यन्ते are tormented, प्राणिनो living beings, मया by me, ते those (diseases), न not, ते you (will affect), प्रभविष्यन्ति will be powerful over, मयि when I am, प्रीते pleased, न not, संशयः doubt.
explanation: Just as other living beings are tormented by various diseases through me, those diseases will not affect you when I am pleased, of this there is no doubt.

shloka_text: मृत्युतस्ते भयं नास्ति वरान्मम विहङ्गम । यावत्त्वां न वधिष्यन्ति नरास्तावद्भविष्यसि ।। 7.18.28 ।।
transliteration: mṛtyutaste bhayaṃ nāsti varānmama vihaṅgama | yāvattvāṃ na vadhiṣyanti narāstāvadbhaviṣyasi || 7.18.28 ||
translation: मृत्युतः from death, ते to you, भयं fear, न नास्ति is not, वरान्मम from my boon, विहङ्गम O bird, यावत्त्वां as long as you, न not, वधिष्यन्ति will kill, नराः humans, तावत् so long, भविष्यसि you will be.
explanation: O bird, you have no fear of death due to my boon; you will continue to exist as long as humans do not kill you.

shloka_text: एते मद्विषयस्था वै मानवाः क्षुद्भयार्दिताः । त्वयि भुक्ते तु तृप्तास्ते भविष्यन्ति सबान्धवाः ।। 7.18.29 ।।
transliteration: ete madviṣayasthā vai mānavāḥ kṣudbhayārditāḥ | tvayi bhukte tu tṛptāste bhaviṣyanti sabāndhavāḥ || 7.18.29 ||
translation: एते these, मद्विषयस्था situated in my realm, वै indeed, मानवाः humans, क्षुद्भयार्दिताः afflicted by the fear of hunger, त्वयि when you, भुक्ते are eaten, तु indeed, तृप्तास्ते satisfied they, भविष्यन्ति will be, सबान्धवाः with their relatives.
explanation: Indeed, these humans in my realm, afflicted by the fear of hunger, will become satisfied along with their relatives when you are eaten.

shloka_text: वरुणस्त्वब्रवीद्धंसं गङ्गातोयविहारिणम् । श्रूयतां प्रीतिसंयुक्तं वचः पत्ररथेश्वर ।। 7.18.30 ।।
transliteration: varuṇastvabravīddhaṃsaṃ gaṅgātoyavihāriṇam | śrūyatāṃ prītisaṃyuktaṃ vacaḥ patraratheśvara || 7.18.30 ||
translation: वरुणः Varuna, तु then, अब्रवीत् said, हंसं to the swan, गङ्गातोयविहारिणम् sporting in the waters of Ganga, श्रूयतां let it be heard, प्रीतिसंयुक्तं filled with affection, वचः words, पत्ररथेश्वर O lord of birds.
explanation: Then Varuna spoke to the swan, who was sporting in the waters of the Ganga, saying, "O lord of birds, listen to these words filled with affection."

shloka_text: वर्णो मनोहरः सौम्यश्चन्द्रमण्डलसन्निभः । भविष्यति तवोदग्रः शुद्धफेनसमप्रभः ।। 7.18.31 ।।
transliteration: varṇo manoharaḥ saumyaścandramaṇḍalasannibhaḥ | bhaviṣyati tavodagraḥ śuddhaphenasamaprabhaḥ || 7.18.31 ||
translation: वर्णो color, मनोहरः charming, सौम्यः gentle, चन्द्रमण्डलसन्निभः resembling the disc of the moon, भविष्यति will be, तव your, उदग्रः excellent, शुद्धफेनसमप्रभः having the luster of pure foam.
explanation: Your complexion will be charming, gentle, resembling the moon's disc, excellent, and will possess the luster of pure foam.

shloka_text: मच्छरीरं समासाद्य कान्तो नित्यं भविष्यसि । प्राप्स्यसे चातुलां प्रीतिमेतन्मे प्रीतिलक्षणम् ।। 7.18.32 ।।
transliteration: maccharīraṃ samāsādya kānto nityaṃ bhaviṣyasi | prāpsyase cātulāṃ prītimetanme prītilakṣaṇam || 7.18.32 ||
translation: मच्छरीरं my body, समासाद्य having obtained, कान्तः beautiful, नित्यं always, भविष्यसि you will be, प्राप्स्यसे you will obtain, च and, अतुलां incomparable, प्रीतिं joy, एतत् this, मे my, प्रीतिलक्षणम् sign of affection.
explanation: By obtaining my body, you will always be beautiful and will attain incomparable joy, for this is a sign of my favor.

shloka_text: हंसानां हि पुरा राम नीलवर्णः सपाण्डुरः । पक्षा नीलाग्रसंवीताः क्रोडाः शष्पाग्रनिर्मलाः ।। 7.18.33 ।।
transliteration: haṃsānāṃ hi purā rāma nīlavarṇaḥ sapāṇḍuraḥ | pakṣā nīlāgrasaṃvītāḥ kroḍāḥ śaṣpāgranirmalāḥ || 7.18.33 ||
translation: हंसानां of swans, हि indeed, पुरा formerly, राम O Rama, नीलवर्णः blue-colored, सपाण्डुरः with a whitish tinge, पक्षाः wings, नीलाग्रसंवीताः covered with blue tips, क्रोडाः breasts, शष्पाग्रनिर्मलाः pure like the tips of fresh grass.
explanation: Indeed, O Rama, in the past, swans were blue-colored with a whitish tinge, their wings were covered with blue tips, and their breasts were pure like the tips of fresh grass.

shloka_text: अथाब्रवीद्वैश्रवणः कृकलासं गिरौ स्थितम् । हैरण्यं सम्प्रयच्छामि वर्णं प्रीतस्तवाप्यहम् ।। 7.18.34 ।।
transliteration: athābravīdvaiśravaṇaḥ kṛkalāsaṃ girau sthitam | hairaṇyaṃ samprayacchāmi varṇaṃ prītastavāpyaham || 7.18.34 ||
translation: अथ then, अब्रवीत् spoke, वैश्रवणः Vaishravana, कृकलासं to the chameleon, गिरौ on the mountain, स्थितम् situated, हैरण्यं golden, सम्प्रयच्छामि I bestow, वर्णं color, प्रीतः pleased, तव to you, अपि also, अहम् I.
explanation: Then Vaishravana, pleased, spoke to the chameleon situated on the mountain, saying, "I bestow upon you a golden color."

shloka_text: सद्रव्यं च शिरो नित्यं भविष्यति तवाक्षयम् । एष काञ्चनको वर्णो मत्प्रीत्या ते भविष्यति ।। 7.18.35 ।।
transliteration: sadravyaṃ ca śiro nityaṃ bhaviṣyati tavākṣayam | eṣa kāñcanako varṇo matprītyā te bhaviṣyati || 7.18.35 ||
translation: सद्रव्यं with wealth, च and, शिरो head, नित्यं always, भविष्यति will be, तव your, अक्षयम् inexhaustible, एष this, काञ्चनकः golden, वर्णः color, मत्प्रीत्या by my favor, ते for you, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: Your head will always be rich and inexhaustible, and this golden color will be yours by my favor.

shloka_text: एवं दत्त्वा वरांस्तेभ्यस्तस्मिन्यज्ञोत्सवे सुराः । निवृत्ताः सह राज्ञा ते पुनः स्वभवनं गताः ।। 7.18.36 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ dattvā varāṃstebhyastasminyajñotsave surāḥ | nivṛttāḥ saha rājñā te punaḥ svabhavanaṃ gatāḥ || 7.18.36 ||
translation: एवं thus, दत्त्वा having given, वरान् boons, तेभ्यः to them, तस्मिन् in that, यज्ञोत्सवे sacrificial festival, सुराः the gods, निवृत्ताः having departed, सह with, राज्ञा the king, ते they, पुनः again, स्वभवनं to their own abodes, गताः went.
explanation: After granting boons to them during that sacrificial festival, the gods, along with the king, returned to their respective abodes. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे ऽष्टादशः सर्गः ।। 18 ।। Thus ends the eighteenth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
